Artificial intelligence isn't the real problem.

item.title: Caris Life Sciences Launches New National Commercial Featuring Jordan Spieth Highlighting the Power of Artificial Intelligence in Early Stage Cancer Detection
item.description:
The new commercial explores how artificial intelligence has transformed golf, analyzing millions of swings and countless data points to help players improve performance.
"Artificial intelligence is transforming nearly every aspect of our lives, from how we work and communicate to how athletes refine their performance," said [David Dean Halbert](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4800371-1&h=873142942&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.carislifesciences.com%2Fbio%2Fdavid-dean-halbert-dsc-hc%2F&a=David+Dean+Halbert), Founder, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Caris Life Sciences. Caris Detect combines comprehensive molecular analysis with advanced artificial intelligence to help create a future where cancer may be detected in early stage, when there is the best chance for cure."
If advanced artificial intelligence can help us understand our golf game, it should also help us better understand our health.
Unlike approaches that evaluate only a limited subset of biomarkers, Caris Detect™ leverages ultra-deep leverages Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) for all 23,000 genes, Whole Transcriptome Sequencing (WTS) and advanced artificial intelligence to analyze the full breadth of cancer-associated molecular signals in both DNA and RNA.
Caris Detect™ is a multi-cancer early detection blood test designed to identify cancer-associated molecular signals using ultra-deep Whole Genome Sequencing, Whole Transcriptome Sequencing and advanced artificial intelligence.

item.title: Consumer apprehension grows as retailers adopt artificial intelligence assisted pricing tools
item.description:
# Consumer apprehension grows as retailers adopt artificial intelligence assisted pricing tools ## Trending Artificial intelligence tools help businesses decide what to charge by predicting how customers might respond.
**Algorithmic pricing gets an assist from AI**
AI can help the software identify patterns in sales, competitors’ prices and other information to predict demand and estimate how different prices would affect sales and profits.
Simon-Kucher, a global consulting company, surveyed more than 2,200 business leaders in 28 countries and 39 industries last year, and 41% said they used AI software to gather market intelligence, including competitors’ prices.
